consequence.statement: Monitoring systems, dashboards, and alerting rules that reference the metric lbipam_ips_used_total will no longer find the metric under its previous name, causing metric collection and alerts to fail or stop reporting.
consequence.remediation: Update all Prometheus scrape configurations, Grafana dashboards, alerting rules, and any monitoring queries to use the new metric name lbipam_ips_used instead of lbipam_ips_used_total.

original.statement: The Cilium metric lbipam_ips_used_total has been renamed to lbipam_ips_used.

consequence.statement: The LB-IPAM IPs-used metric is now exposed as lbipam_ips_used, not lbipam_ips_used_total. Monitoring that refers to the old name should be checked against the new name.
consequence.remediation: Review Prometheus queries, recording/alerting rules and dashboards that reference lbipam_ips_used_total and update them to lbipam_ips_used.

corrected.statement: In Cilium 1.17.0 the metric lbipam_ips_used_total is renamed to lbipam_ips_used (listed under Changed Metrics). The metric is still exposed under the new name. Queries, dashboards or alerts that use the old name should be checked.

decision.reason: [ev-1bf87d491deb] only says, under "Changed Metrics", that `lbipam_ips_used_total` has been renamed to `lbipam_ips_used`. It does not say that any configured setting stops being honoured or that monitoring fails. A metric name is not an operator setting, so setting-ignored and its "high" severity claim more mandatory work than the evidence supports. The metric is still emitted under a new name, so consumers that query the old name should be reviewed. That makes this a behavior-change (review) rather than an action-required failure.
